_note: Seeded from Worldbuilding/Ephemer/World Map Reference.md. Every x/y here is a v0 eyeball estimate read off the OLD map image, and none is right for the art this section serves — that render draws Vestur about half again as wide and sets Austur further west, so a pin at its seeded coordinate can land in open water. The DM drags each pin where it belongs; that writes a row to map_locations and the row is the truth from then on. These numbers are a starting position, never a claim. The server filters this file before serving it: a location with secret:true is withheld from players until the DM reveals it.

locations.name: Aurus
locations.note: The city where gold flows. Eight districts, each held by a Grand Family and each selling one thing completely — war, magic, pleasure, food, records, loans, entertainment, and the expeditions that go out past the map. Nothing here is given and nothing is forbidden; there is only the price, and the rule that your word outranks your coin. Every twenty-five years the **Golden Rush** decides who owns the place next. Governor: Induz Hightower.

locations.name: Synka
locations.note: The quiet city at the northern tip, and the Aurus family's own. The greatest gold mine in the world was found under Synka; the mine has been empty for a long time now. The family that gave the nation its name still has a say here, and nowhere else, and the town is known chiefly for being peaceful. Leader: Andeline Aurus.

locations.name: Brok
locations.note: Before the Golden Canal, every ship that mattered put in at Brok. Then Aurus dug its own way to the sea and kept the tolls. Brok is still a port; it is simply no longer *the* port, and the difference shows in the warehouses. Leader: Jonas Irivos.

locations.name: Schnauz
locations.note: A port on the southwestern coast, built by the Schnauz family with the winnings of their Golden Rush. They ruled their twenty-five years, handed the nation on, and retired here to rule something smaller that would stay theirs. Leader: Gerarld Schnauz.

locations.name: Old Pine
locations.note: The city that takes what Aurus throws away. An anonymous donor delivered an **Aeon Crystal** here in **2847**, and four years later a wandering priest of Faye named the great pine at its centre divine — one of the original **Seeds of the Gardener**, which would never wither nor could be cut. Around those two facts grew the Second-Chance Market: those who cannot pay Aurus's trading fee come here to sell cheaper. Leader: Camille Rose.

locations.name: Villie
locations.note: Aurus's embassy to the dark. What cannot legally be sold above is sold in Villie, which is the whole of its purpose and the whole of its problem — the trade draws exactly the people the trade would draw. Leader: Silas Enderwill.

locations.name: Anerolt
locations.note: North, where the cold reaches from toes to head and the sky stays clouded, stands the **Black Gate**: sixty feet tall, two hundred wide, and two Noirs above it deciding whether you are a visitor or a meal. Past it is the largest city in Vestur, so large it does not feel like one city — five sections, each under its own Aeon Crystal, from the castle at A-ONE to the suburbs at D-FOUR and E-FIVE, with the arcane college **Arcanus Maxima** at C-THREE. You are always being watched, by the guard or by The Shade, and the city's one manner is not to ask.

locations.name: Lionhearth
locations.note: The largest settlement in Ephemer, and nobody ever decided it should be. Raised with the kingdom in **Year -55**, Lionhearth has been added to by all forty of its monarchs and emptied by none of them — a fortress, a court, an order of knights, a gallery, an archive, a tomb, each one the thing some reign required and every one of them still standing, still staffed, still funded. The city has no districts so much as **strata**: walk from the palace to the south wall and you walk forward through three thousand years. A crown enchanted to hover above the rooftops in 2476 is still up there, because no successor has been willing to be the one who brings it down.

locations.name: Coldspire
locations.note: Far north in the snowfields, where the blood still runs **Azure** — the old blue light of Vuitheus's children, surfacing generations later in a people who never entirely stopped being something else. **House Veridian** answers the Crown when it suits them, and nobody when it doesn't.

locations.name: Dust
locations.note: Northeast, where the snow behaves like sand and the cold does the work a desert's heat would. A halfling artificer keeps it under a **Fragment** — the thinnest shield in the kingdom's north.

locations.name: Last Bastion
locations.note: The wall the Azurians never passed. House Greyhawk has held it ever since, and the lord who sits here is also **Arch General of Valentis** — which makes Last Bastion less a city than the army's own address. The kingdom's highest soldier does not live in its capital; he lives at the top of the northern road.

locations.name: The Ridge
locations.note: The pass itself, fortified — and, simply, **the gate of Lionhearth**. Whoever holds the Ridge holds the capital's front door, and no column reaches the throne while it stands. Beatrice Bristow garrisoned it for the better part of two decades before she was given Acer; a Blakesleye holds it now, for the King.

locations.name: Darkwatch
locations.note: Where Valentis keeps the magic it will not do anywhere else. East of the pass, chaotic-magic experiments run under a dwarven monk's eye, while his brother **Beiron** handles what comes of them.

locations.name: Willowstead
locations.note: The **Great Willow** is older than the dukedom and taller than the keep, and every Sparrow child learns to climb it before they learn to bow. Willowstead flies **Argos-era banners** on festival days, refuses new honours, and sings the old songs loudly and on purpose. Its duke knows every family in the city by name and grievance. The Crown lets the mourning stand — hanging a beloved duke for a song would only water the rumour it most needs dead.

locations.name: Acer
locations.note: The maple sprouted here once and nowhere else on the continent, and the city grew around that miracle the way sugar crystallizes — slowly, sweetly, in layers. Acer smells of caramel from its gates to its quay, and ships syrup barrels stamped for every table in Vestur. It is beloved, unthreatening, and audited by no one, which is the most useful thing about it.

locations.name: Misthold
locations.note: West-central, in the forests near the Jägenberg border. A city that appeared faster than cities appear, run by a warlock, and nobody in Valentis asks the follow-up question.

locations.name: Crimson Edge
locations.note: The kingdom's newest edge, by the great lake, taken from Faenys in the war and still not digested — a southern band full of people who remember flying another flag. Its lord is sworn to the late **King Argos**.

locations.name: Fang
locations.note: The southern tip of the eastern lobe, and the kingdom's anvil: a smith town arming the army its holder's own house commands.

locations.name: Aquilus
locations.note: The desert capital, entered through a Traders Gate no one passes without a permit and a Caravanserai where the wagons sleep. Its life runs between the **Grand Souq** and **The Warren** — wealth and want a street apart — and its faith around the **Crystal Temple** and the **Sunstone Obelisk**, the Prime Pillar of Ikar. It stands where it stands for two reasons: the ring of mountains that shields it, and the subterranean river that makes life possible in an arid land. Home of the Golden Wings and the academy where Chocobo mounted combat is taught. Ruler: Regent Queen Layla Aquilus.

locations.name: Old Point
locations.note: Old Point is the oldest city in Talon and, by the record, the oldest on the continent — it goes back to the age of the Giants. Scholars keep coming to dig at it, hoping what is buried here is useful. Leader: Tantor.

locations.name: Ashenwall
locations.note: A volcano burst here long ago and left the soil behind, and Ashenwall has been growing the best produce in Talon out of that ash ever since. It is also home to the **Ashen Blades**, run by the Flameheart family — Thorin, who led mercenaries before he led a guild, Kara, whose spells gave the company its name, and Liora, who decides which work is taken. Leader: Paige Baylee.

locations.name: Shimmerwing
locations.note: Talon's green city, and its loudest. An underground river gives Shimmerwing the best farmland in the nation, and the feed makes it the nation's **chocobo country** — more breeders here than anywhere in Talon. Eight names are called at the line — Blue Storm, Bumblebee, The Blurred Shadow, Kimeko, Blossom, Rain Step, Daredevil and Silvara — and the odds move with who is absent. Leader: Dominic Alvard.

locations.name: Tryad
locations.note: Three towers stand over Tryad — **Sapphire**, **Emerald** and **Ruby** — and the city sorts itself by their colours, down to which inn a traveller is pointed toward. It was founded by the first friends Cecil Aquilus made in the desert, and three of their descendants rule it still, one to a tower: Bronann, Disin and Chaval. Scholars have been arriving since the temple was found.

locations.name: Sunwater
locations.note: The nation's front door. Everyone entering Talon comes through Sunwater first, which makes it a merchant's city and a magnet for trouble — with that many strangers passing through, Talon's code is the one thing that does not travel well. Leader: Theresa Radcliffe.

locations.name: The Grand Temple of Vestur
locations.note: Neutral city-state on the mainland.

locations.name: Jägenberg
locations.note: The peak of every craft in Vestur is in this one city, and the reason is in the floor: the three founders dug until they struck lava and brought it up, and the **Great Forge Insinerus** has been burning on it ever since. The Three Lords rule from here — Halvard of Clan Breith, Sigrid of Clan Fell, Trond of Clan Hallr — and when all three are away in their own cities the nation answers to **The Eyes of the Lords**. Lordships are not inherited; they are taken in the **Trials of Steel**. *Born free, die free.*

locations.name: Breith
locations.note: Founded by **Breith**, eldest of the three siblings, and still the clan's seat. Breith makes things — weapons, tools, and whatever else the nation needs built next. Held by Halvard of Clan Breith, the **Lord of Crafting**.

locations.name: Hallstein
locations.note: The builders' city, founded by **Hallr**. Hallstein's trade is construction itself, and it is good enough at it that other nations hire its people to build for them. Held by Trond of Clan Hallr, the **Lord of Building**.

locations.name: Merk
locations.note: Not one of the three great clans, and it does not need to be. Merk teaches fighting, and the greatest warriors of the nation have come here to learn it. Held by Arne of Clan Merk.

locations.name: Kor
locations.note: Clan Kor brews. It will never win them a lordship and everyone knows it, and everyone also knows that without the ale nobody in Jägenberg would work at their peak. Held by Ragna of Clan Kor.

locations.name: Fellstrong
locations.note: Founded by **Fell**, the sister, and sunk into mining the way the others sank into craft and stone. Fellstrong has driven shafts into the largest deposits of precious metal and ore the nation knows. Held by Sigrid of Clan Fell, the **Lord of Mining**.

locations.name: Zeros
locations.note: A city under the ground, and once home to thousands of drow who became the best there are at surviving down there. A remaining drow family commands it still and trains its people the same way. Leader: Ariadne Hexditch. *The surface marker is the way in.*

locations.name: Faenys
locations.note: The capital came down out of the sky with everything else, and the dynasty's first act was to put it back — rebuilt on its own wreckage in under a year, which is either resilience or denial depending on who you ask. Its **Rose Blooms** open at the start of spring and cover the city. Here stand the college of magic and arts **Arcane Sonata**, and the sword school **Wind Dancers**. Ruler: Emperor Arovan Faenys.

locations.name: Tyff
locations.note: The newest town in Vestur. When Valentis took the city of **Aelia**, the survivors of the raid carried out the last shard of its Aeon Crystal and ran south. Where they stopped, they made a safe haven; a year later it is a town with a name. Leader: Vilroth Trislamin.

locations.name: Asyfall
locations.note: A wall, a garrison, and four hundred years of answering *what are we standing on* with the word **foundations** and then changing the subject. Asyfall was built by the survivors of Aethereach's fall, on the wreck itself; it dug into the ruin once, at the founding, to seat its Aeon Crystal, and swore never to go down again. Here, mourning Aethereach is not forbidden — it is embarrassing. Trains scouts and warriors of silence.

locations.name: Caell
locations.note: The city of hunters. Nobody tracks or tames a beast better than Caell does, and the city has made that the whole of its reputation. It stands, like the capital, on a sky-city that fell. Leader: Tibal Neriphine.

locations.name: Nivelleth
locations.note: Nivelleth was founded to research a new kind of magic. Rumour says that research produced two things: the orcs, and the great crater. Leader: Esra Olavaris.

locations.name: Isfaren
locations.note: The nation's larder — the largest farmland in Faenys, and the reason the dynasty still eats. Druids come here and are treated like royalty, on one condition, which is that they help with the work. Leader: Adol Roven.

locations.name: Wollniege
locations.note: One of the **six kingdoms the world began with**, founded by the gnome inventor **Carmyn Wollniege** and a republic ever since. The city stands in the canopy of the Mushroom Jungle, on a coast, with its gates shut and its workshops open — the most technologically advanced place in Ephemer, where machine and magic are built into one another rather than beside each other. What leaves Wollniege is rare and astonishing. What gets in is supposed to be nothing at all.

locations.name: Skippingmire
locations.note: West.

locations.name: Nelrima
locations.note: South.

locations.name: Tivan — Paradise
locations.note: The turtle-shaped island of the northern Freetides, bearing the settlement Paradise. Not Titan Island, which is hidden and appears on no map.

locations.name: The Scorched Lands
locations.note: Volcanic island wreathed by the Steaming Depths. The old map prints "The Scorshed Island"; the canonical name is Juan's ruling.

locations.name: The Rusted Justicar
locations.note: A great sword driven into a stone islet at the centre of the Dead Waters — the only marked feature in Austur's interior sea.

locations.name: Vesper Gulch
locations.note: Referenced in Chapter 2 — Dreams of Violet Sand, and drawn on no map. This position is an estimate awaiting a ruling, which is why it starts hidden: the guess is the secret, not the place.
